newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Robotics to offer Internet over cable.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Robotics to offer Internet over cable.

text.p: U.S. Robotics Corp. said Monday it is introducing a system for providing Internet access over cable television networks.

The computer modem maker, which agreed at the end of last month to merge with Local Area Network technology company 3Com Corp. in a $7.3 billion stock deal, said its cable access system provides operators with a new way to deliver data over cable quickly and cost-effectively.
The new cable access system is designed for rapid deployment, as well as long-term flexibility for cable operators, U.S. Robotics said in a statement.
U.S. Robotics said it created a Cable Access Business Unit and will demonstrate the new system March 17-19 at the National Cable Television Association Cable 97 trade show in New Orleans.
U.S. Robotics said its Cable Access Business Unit is in talks with cable operators and expects to begin technical and field trials this summer, with widespread availability to follow in the fall.
The two-way cable access system is expected to be available in early 1998, it said.

"With the introduction of our new cable access system, we offer a headend solution that is based on our proven Total Control network platform," said Casey Cowell, chairman and chief executive officer of U.S. Robotics.

"Further, our approach is designed to eliminate the inhibitors to a mass market for cable modems and establish a true retail environment. This strategic approach dramatically reduces capital costs at every point in the network and makes cable Internet access a far more practical reality," he said in a statement.
U.S. Robotics stock was up $1.25 cents at $57.625 in morning trading on Nasdaq.
